textbookText: 91. Boyle's Law states that, at constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is: A) Inversely proportional to its volume (PV = constant) B) Directly proportional to its volume C) Independent of its volume D) Proportional to the square of its volume

92. Charles's Law states that, at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is: A) Directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V/T = constant) B) Inversely proportional to its absolute temperature C) Independent of temperature D) Proportional to the square of temperature

93. Gay-Lussac's Law (pressure law) states that, at constant volume, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is: A) Directly proportional to its absolute temperature (P/T = constant) B) Inversely proportional to its absolute temperature C) Independent of temperature D) Proportional to volume
94. The combined gas law, merging Boyle's, Charles's, and Gay-Lussac's laws, is expressed as: A) PV/T = constant B) PV × T = constant C) P + V + T = constant D) P/VT = constant
95. The ideal gas equation is written as: A) PV = nRT B) PV = nR/T C) P/V = nRT D) PT = nRV

96. Avogadro's law (relevant to gas laws) states that, at constant temperature and pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to: A) The number of moles of gas present B) The molar mass of the gas C) The pressure applied D) The nature (identity) of the gas

97. Dalton's Law of partial pressures states that the total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases equals: A) The sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas in the mixture B) The average of the partial pressures C) The partial pressure of the gas with the highest molar mass only D) The product of all partial pressures

98. Graham's Law of diffusion states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is: A) Inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass (or density) B) Directly proportional to its molar mass C) Independent of molar mass D) Directly proportional to the square root of its molar mass
99. According to Boyle's law, if the volume of a fixed mass of gas is halved at constant temperature, its pressure will: A) Double B) Halve C) Remain the same D) Quadruple
100. STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure) conditions are defined as: A) 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm (101.325 kPa) pressure B) 25°C and 2 atm C) 100°C and 1 atm D) 0 K and 0 atm

101. An extraordinary historical fact about Boyle's Law is that it was: A) One of the earliest quantitative gas laws (1662), based on experiments with a J-shaped tube of trapped air B) Derived purely from Bohr's atomic theory C) Proven false by later kinetic theory D) Discovered using only theoretical calculation, without any experiment

102. Why does a balloon expand when taken from a cold room to a warm room at roughly constant pressure (application of gas laws)? A) Charles's law — volume increases proportionally with absolute temperature at constant pressure B) Boyle's law — volume increases as pressure decreases C) Dalton's law — partial pressures increase D) Graham's law — diffusion rate increases

103. The gas constant R in the ideal gas equation has the value approximately: A) 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (or 0.0821 L·atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹) B) 6.022 × 10²³ J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ C) 22.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ D) 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (this is actually Boltzmann's constant, a distractor)

104. Which of the gas laws would explain why a pressure cooker cooks food faster? A) Gay-Lussac's law — increased temperature at constant (sealed) volume raises pressure, raising the boiling point of water B) Boyle's law — decreased pressure lowers boiling point C) Charles's law — volume increase lowers temperature D) Graham's law — faster diffusion of steam
105. The value of absolute zero, as derived by extrapolating Charles's law graphs (V vs T) to zero volume, is approximately: A) −273.15°C B) 0°C C) −100°C D) 100°C

106. Real gases deviate from ideal gas behavior most significantly under conditions of: A) High pressure and low temperature B) Low pressure and high temperature C) STP conditions exactly D) Zero pressure only

107. According to Graham's law, a lighter gas (lower molar mass) diffuses: A) Faster than a heavier gas under the same conditions B) Slower than a heavier gas C) At the same rate as any other gas D) Only if it is a noble gas

108. Which application demonstrates Dalton's law of partial pressures in real life (extraordinary/practical fact)? A) Calculating the partial pressure of oxygen at high altitude to understand why breathing becomes difficult (lower total & partial pressures) B) Explaining why solids do not mix C) Explaining capillary rise in narrow tubes D) Explaining why ice floats on water

109. In the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, if temperature and moles are constant, doubling the pressure will: A) Halve the volume (Boyle's law behavior) B) Double the volume C) Leave the volume unchanged D) Quadruple the volume
